Mildly positive and data-dependent. The Committee underscores strong labor markets and inflation near its symmetric 2% PCE objective, while keeping policy “accommodative” and signaling further gradual hikes. Relative to Taylor-rule benchmarks and a low estimated natural rate of unemployment, maintaining the funds rate below the long-run level is consistent with measured tightening and expectation management in the literature. Low market-based inflation compensation suggests anchored long-term expectations, reducing near-term inflation risk. At the same time, VAR evidence (e.g., Sims, 1992) and the “price puzzle” caution against overreacting to short-run inflation moves, supporting gradualism and a balanced-risk stance. The ongoing balance-sheet normalization (capped reinvestments in Treasuries and agency MBS) aligns with evidence that QE primarily works through the monetary base and term premia, allowing the policy rate to remain the main tool as inflation hovers near target. Overall tone: confident but cautious.
